problem: Find the equation of the downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(4,0)$ and which passes through the point $(1,-4).$
worked_solution:
For any upward or downward-opening parabola with its vertex at $(h,k),$ the general standard equation is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Here, the vertex has coordinates $(h,k)=(4,0).$ Substituting these into the general standard equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2} & =4py.\end{aligned}
$$

We are left to find the value of $p.$ We know that the given parabola also passes through the point $(1,-4),$ so we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=-4$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2} & =4py \\ (1-4)^{2} & =4p(-4) \\ 9 & =-16p \\ p & =-\frac{9}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2} & =4py \\ (x-4)^{2} & =4(-\frac{9}{16})y \\ (x-4)^{2} & =-\frac{9}{4}y.\end{aligned}
$$
